title: Saving Foundation Flow-Matching Priors for Inverse Problems
claim: Standard plug-in methods search from scratch in seed space; a warm start shortcuts the search trajectory toward the feasible set.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, (a) prior vs (b) ours, dashed vertical maps between spaces
description: Two side-by-side geometric diagrams compare the standard plug-in approach (a) with FMPlug (b). Each panel has an orange wavy band for the image manifold and a green cloud for the feasible set {x|y=A(x)} at the top. Red dots linked by purple arrows form the image trajectory. Pink arrows form a seed-space trajectory at the bottom, and gray dashed vertical arrows labeled G_θ map seed points to image points. In (a), the search starts at z_0 and moves step by step through seed space, with the caption that search in the seed space induces search in the image manifold. In (b), dotted lines run from the seed points z_0 to the measurement y near the feasible set. They give instance-guided warm-start points z_{α_t}. The note says warm start can shortcut the search trajectory. Gradient formulas sit under each panel. Panel labels (a) Plug-in approach and (b) Our FMPlug are at the bottom.
caption: Illustration of the general plug-in approach (left) and our FMPlug method (right) for solving IPs with pretrained foundation FM priors.
abstract: Foundation flow-matching (FM) models promise universal priors for solving inverse problems (IPs); yet today, they trail behind domain-specific and even untrained priors. \emph{How can we unlock their potential?} We introduce FMPlug, a plug-in framework that redefines how foundation FMs are used in IPs. FMPlug combines an instance-guided, time-dependent warm-start strategy with sharp Gaussianity regularization, adding problem-specific guidance while preserving the Gaussian structures. For evaluation, we consider both simple image restoration tasks and scientific IPs with a few similar samples -- where the prohibitive cost of data collection and model training hinders the development of domain-specific generative models. Our superior experimental results confirm the effectiveness of FMPlug. Overall, FMPlug paves the way for making foundation FM models practical, reusable priors for IPs, especially scientific ones with few similar samples. More details are available at https://sun-umn.github.io/xm-plug/ .
